uncataloged.reason: Genuine bug confirmed in code, new file introduced by this diff (cmd/hooks/skill-invoke-gate.sh, new in this range per git diff). Line 42: `case "$first_user" in "/$required"*) invoked=1 ;; *) invoked="" ;; esac` is a bare glob prefix match with no word-boundary — a required name that is a string-prefix of another skill's slash-invocation (e.g. required="smine", first_user="/smine-batch ...") satisfies the case pattern and marks the gate invoked without the actual required skill having loaded. This is a distinct root cause from all six golden findings on this file (GV3-132/138/152/159/166/170), none of which address the prompt-start prefix-match branch.

Technically accurate and in new code introduced by this diff (styleTestTarget, internal/server/profilesettings.go, confirmed new via git diff): `labeledPath := filepath.Join(s.tokenDir, label)` joins the routine's ROUTINE_TOKEN env value with no filepath.Clean/prefix containment check before os.Stat and later feeding the file's contents to claude -p as an OAuth token. Currently low-severity since label comes from admin-configured routine env (routines.Scan), not attacker-controlled input, which the finding itself concedes ("if that env ever becomes reachable from a less-trusted input path") — a defensive-coding observation on an existing trust boundary, not a proven exploit today. No golden entry on this file addresses path validation of the token label (GV3-051 covers untested model/token resolution, a different root cause).
